facts.fact_text: The applicants and some other people (several dozen in total) disagreed with the course of action of demolishing Voronezh municipal market and building a shopping centre, which would adversely affect their businesses and employment.
The applicants and some other people (several dozen in total) decided to remain on the Voronezh municipal market premises permanently, doing 'night shifts'.
The entrepreneurs started their 'night shifts' at Voronezh municipal market on an unspecified date.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Annenkov was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khripunov was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khavantsev was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Finskiy was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Suprunova was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Zakharova was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Guseva was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
At 5.30 a.m. on 10 August 2009 the police arrested some twenty people at Voronezh municipal market.
Among those arrested at 5.30 a.m. on 10 August 2009 at Voronezh municipal market were applicants Mr Buzov, Ms Garkavets, Ms Zhuravleva, Ms Khavantseva and Ms Suprunova.
Ms Yef., the applicants' colleague, made a written statement that in the early morning of 7 August 2009 some thirty people had been at Voronezh municipal market.
Officer Ku. stated that the officers saw some twenty people outside the building who were holding a meeting, chanting slogans and shouting about the regional prosecutor and the governor.

The Federal Law on Gatherings, Meetings, Demonstrations, Processions and Pickets, no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), provides that a public event is an open, peaceful event accessible to all, organised at the initiative of citizens of the Russian Federation, political parties, other public associations, or religious associations.

The Federal Law on Gatherings, Meetings, Demonstrations, Processions and Pickets, no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004 (the Public Events Act), defines a 'gathering' (собрание) as an assembly of citizens in a specially designated or arranged location for the purpose of the collective discussion of socially important issues (section 2(2) of the Public Events Act).
On 6 August 2009 the police told the entrepreneurs who had gathered at Voronezh municipal market to leave the premises.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Annenkov was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khripunov was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khavantsev was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Finskiy was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Suprunova was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Zakharova was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
On 7 August 2009 Ms Guseva was arrested at Voronezh municipal market.
By a judgment of 7 August 2009 a justice of the peace convicted Mr Finskiy of an offence under Article 19.3 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
The justice of the peace sentenced Mr Finskiy to five days' administrative detention by judgment of 7 August 2009.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khripunov was sentenced to five days' administrative detention by a justice of the peace.
Mr Khavantsev was sentenced to ten days' administrative detention.
At 5.30 a.m. on 10 August 2009 the police arrested some twenty people at Voronezh municipal market.
Among those arrested at 5.30 a.m. on 10 August 2009 at Voronezh municipal market were applicants Mr Buzov, Ms Garkavets, Ms Zhuravleva, Ms Khavantseva and Ms Suprunova.
By a judgment of 10 August 2009 Mr Buzov was convicted of an offence under Article 19.3 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
Mr Buzov was sentenced to ten days' administrative detention by the justice of the peace by judgment of 10 August 2009.

Mr Finskiy, Mr Khavantsev and Mr Khripunov were accused of an offence under Article 19.3 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO), which punished disobeying or resisting the lawful order of a public official.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Finskiy violated the procedure for organising and managing a gathering (собрание).
The justice of the peace held that Mr Khripunov violated the procedure for organising and managing a gathering.

The Deputy President of the Voronezh Regional Court dismissed the defence's argument that the lower courts' judges had omitted to specify the type of public event in which the defendants had participated, the relevant regulations on such public events, and the specific details concerning the police's orders to the defendants, stating that it had been established by the justice of the peace that the impugned event was a 'gathering'.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Mr Annenkov that neither the record of the administrative offence nor the judgment contained references to specific circumstances or actions relating to the corpus delicti of the imputed offence of disobeying the lawful order of a police officer, and in particular neither document specified what order was given to Mr Annenkov which was then not complied with, and the judgment did not indicate that Mr Annenkov had disobeyed a lawful order issued by a police officer.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Guseva that the record of the administrative offence did not specify what type of public event was being held, which procedure was violated, or what orders relating to maintaining public order during a public event were not complied with by Ms Guseva.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Suprunova that the record of the administrative offence did not indicate what type of public event was being held, which applicable procedure Ms Suprunova allegedly violated, what orders relating to maintaining public order during such an event were issued to Ms Suprunova by the police, or which of those orders was not complied with.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Zakharova that neither the record of the administrative offence nor the first-instance judgment referred to specific facts and actions forming part of the offence imputed to Ms Zakharova of disobeying the lawful order of a police officer, or the specific order given to her which she failed to comply with, and the record did not specify what Ms Zakharova's violation of the procedure concerning the organisation and management of demonstrations, meetings and gatherings was, or what type of event was being held.

Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova argued in their application for review that the lower courts had not specified what specific order Mr Buzov had disobeyed or whether such an order was lawful under Russian law.
Mr Buzov and his counsel Ms Gnezdilova argued in their application for review that the courts had not specified any particular actions on Mr Buzov's part which constituted a breach of public order.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Zhuravleva that the record of the administrative offence did not specify which requests relating to public order were addressed to Ms Zhuravleva and were not complied with, or which actions of Ms Zhuravleva such requests related to, and that the deficiencies of the record made it impossible to establish Ms Zhuravleva's liability for an administrative offence, and the record must be returned to the police.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh held in respect of Ms Khavantseva and Ms Garkavets that neither the record of the administrative offence nor the justice of the peace's judgment specified how each defendant violated public order, or which specific order was given by the police in this connection but not complied with by her.

At the material time, Article 19.3 § 1 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO) punished with a fine or administrative detention the following behaviour: disobeying the lawful order of a police officer, a military officer or a detention facility staff member in relation to the fulfilment of their official duties aimed at securing public order and public safety.

At the material time, Article 19.3 § 1 of the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO) also punished with a fine or administrative detention resisting the fulfilment of such duties by police officers, military officers or detention facility staff members.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Finskiy disobeyed a lawful order issued by police officers in relation to their duties to ensure public order and safety.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Finskiy obstructed police officers' exercise of their duties to ensure public order and safety.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Khripunov disobeyed a lawful order issued by police officers in relation to their duties to ensure public order and safety.
The justice of the peace held that Mr Khripunov obstructed police officers' exercise of their duties to ensure public order and safety.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh dismissed the argument that the police had acted unlawfully in relation to the entrepreneurs' presence at a gathering requiring no prior authorisation, finding that the police had acted lawfully with the aim of ensuring public order and public safety because the entrepreneurs were blocking access to the market for employees and had not reacted to lawful orders from the police to stop these actions.

The Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh dismissed the defence's argument that Mr Khripunov had lawfully participated in a gathering requiring no prior authorisation, finding that the police's actions were lawful and aimed to secure public order and public safety since the entrepreneurs were blocking the market employees' access to the building.

The Deputy President of the Voronezh Regional Court held that Mr Buzov was part of the group of people who impeded market officials as they tried to gain access to their office building, that guards from a private security company intervened and a fight ensued between them and some participants, that these participants did not respond to orders from police officers, and that the officers required Mr Buzov, who was one of the most active participants, to cease his unlawful conduct, but he did not respond to this order, and was thereafter taken to the police station.
Officer Ku. stated that at 5.45 a.m. on 7 August 2009 some thirty officers under his supervision arrived at Voronezh municipal market to prevent disorder and unlawful actions.
The justice of the peace sentenced Mr Finskiy to five days' administrative detention by judgment of 7 August 2009.
On 7 August 2009 Mr Khripunov was sentenced to five days' administrative detention by a justice of the peace.
Mr Khavantsev was sentenced to ten days' administrative detention.
Mr Khripunov and Mr Finskiy argued before the Sovetskiy District Court of Voronezh that the penalty of administrative detention had been disproportionate.
Mr Buzov was sentenced to ten days' administrative detention by the justice of the peace by judgment of 10 August 2009.

The penalty of administrative detention under the Federal Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO) could only be imposed by a court and only in exceptional circumstances, when a less intrusive penalty such as a fine would not be appropriate.
